title: Bible Parable: Seeds on Different Ground
subtheme: Bible Parable: Seeds on Different Ground
description: A planting story compares seeds falling on several kinds of ground. Optional Bible interest: Mark 4:1–20.

solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Person scattering seeds to plant them
Plant part from which a new plant grows
Sharp point on a rose stem

answerNotes.SEED: Plant part from which a new plant grows. This scene follows Mark 4:1–20; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.SOIL: Soil is the material around garden roots. It contains more than loose mineral particles: air, water, and decaying material are also part of it.
answerNotes.PATH: A path is a route for walking. Stepping stones can mark that route without making a continuous paved surface.
answerNotes.ROCK: Rock is natural solid material. Pebble usually means a small piece, especially one rounded by moving water.
answerNotes.BIRD: Birds have feathers, beaks, and wings. Not every bird flies, so feathers are a more dependable identifying feature than flight alone.
answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star. Its closeness makes it look much larger and brighter than the points of light seen at night.
answerNotes.ROOT: Roots anchor a plant and take up water from the soil. They are below the stem, even when part of a root is visible above ground.
answerNotes.SOWER: Person scattering seeds to plant them. This scene follows Mark 4:1–20; the passage gives the story's context.

answerNotes.MUSTARD: Plant with a tiny seed in a familiar parable. This scene follows Matthew 13:31–32; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.SEED: Small starting part planted in soil. This scene follows Matthew 13:31–32; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.GARDEN: A garden is an area cultivated for plants. A single bed or plot can be one part of a larger garden.
answerNotes.BRANCH: A branch is a woody limb extending from a tree or shrub. A twig is usually a smaller, thinner piece of that growth.
answerNotes.BIRD: Birds have feathers, beaks, and wings. Not every bird flies, so feathers are a more dependable identifying feature than flight alone.
answerNotes.NEST: A nest is a place for eggs and young. Many birds build nests, but the materials and locations differ from one species to another.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.
answerNotes.SOIL: Soil is the material around garden roots. It contains more than loose mineral particles: air, water, and decaying material are also part of it.
answerNotes.SHELTER: A bus shelter protects waiting passengers from some weather. It does not replace checking the route or arrival information.

answerNotes.SHEEP: Farm animal known for its woolly fleece. This scene follows Luke 15:1–7; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.LOST: Unable to be found. This scene follows Luke 15:1–7; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.SHEPHERD: A shepherd tends a flock of sheep. The Bible uses both real shepherds in its stories and shepherd imagery in its teachings.
answerNotes.HOME: Home can mean a dwelling or the local side in a sporting match. Read the clue before applying the familiar household meaning.

answerNotes.COIN: Small metal piece of money. This scene follows Luke 15:8–10; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.LAMP: A lamp provides light from a fuel or electrical source. Bible lamps used oil rather than a modern bulb.
answerNotes.HOUSE: A house is a building. Home is the place associated with living and belonging, which need not be a separate house.
answerNotes.TEN: Ten is the number associated with the commandments. The puzzle uses the familiar count, not memorization of their order.
answerNotes.LIGHT: Light makes things visible. A lamp produces light, while a mirror mainly reflects light arriving from elsewhere.
answerNotes.SWEEP: To gather loose floor debris with a broom. This scene follows Luke 15:8–10; the passage gives the story's context.

answerNotes.SON: Male child in a family. This scene follows Luke 15:11–32; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.HOME: One's own house or dwelling. This scene follows Luke 15:11–32; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.ROAD: A road is a route for vehicles. A sidewalk or footpath provides a different part of the journey for people on foot.
answerNotes.ROBE: A robe is a loose outer garment. In a Bible story it is clothing, not a separate kind of blanket or tablecloth.
answerNotes.FEAST: A feast is a large celebratory meal. The meal's role depends on its story, such as welcoming a guest or celebrating a return.
answerNotes.SHARE: Share means give part of something to others. In a meal setting it can concern food rather than dividing property or money.
answerNotes.LOST: Lost describes what cannot currently be found. The three Luke 15 parables use different missing things to tell related stories of return and joy.
